newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French stocks hammered, other bourses fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French stocks hammered, other bourses fall.

text.p: Jittery investors hammered French stocks on Wednesday after it appeared the opposition Socialists may be well placed for Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections and other major European bourses fell.
The French rout came after rumours swept the market about privately commissioned polls.

At one point the Paris bourse was down 4.4 percent, but the CAC-40 index picked itself off the floor in the afternoon as much of the rest of Europe's equity markets went into reverse. Several stock markets bubbled to fresh trading highs during the morning, but a combination of weakening bond markets and a negative start on Wall Street damaged sentiment.
The currency market saw the dollar edge lower against the mark and yen, although there was little impact seen from slightly stronger than expected U.S. durable goods data.
Platinum and palladium prices also soared to fresh highs on news of a strike at Anglo American Platinum Corp's Rustenburg mine in South Africa.

"The market has gone crazy. The market is very, very tight," said one dealer as palladium was fixed in London at a record $188.00 in the morning, although it slipped back to $186 at the afternoon fix.
The French stock market provided the main drama, however, with the CAC-40 index falling the largest amount in percentage terms in four years before struggling off its lows.
By 1415 GMT the blue chip benchmark was down 84 points, or 3.13 percent, at 2,596.34 after hitting a low of 2,561.23.

One French trader said the market was being bombarded by rumours and, with more private polls due on Thursday on the likely outcome of the National Assembly elections, the bourse was feeling fragile. The poll findings cannot be divulged under French law.
"There are significant market concerns over the prospect of the Socialists winning the election," Mike Young, director of European investment strategy at Goldman Sachs in London.

Share analysts have estimated the CAC could fall to between 2,450 and 2,500 if the left won. But if the Socialists took an outright majority they would not need to rely on the Communists for votes and would be able to pursue more centrist policies.
Although several European stock markets pushed their way into record territory during the morning, the good times could not last.
Germany's 30-share DAX index pushed to a new trading high of 3,632.33 in early trade but went into retreat after failing to penetrate the psychologically important 3,700-point level.
The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade down 37.94 points at 3,636.42. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX was down 24.93 points at 3,640.50 ahead of a holiday on Thursday.
Traders said the holiday and nervousness about the French election made them reluctant to take fresh positions.
London investors were also cheered initially by Wall Street's strong performance on Tuesday, but went into a decline as events in France hit European bonds.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index was down eight points at 4,673 by mid-afternoon.
"Rising (interest) rates around the world are not helping. People are feeling a bit cautious, as they should. We've had a very good run," said one dealer.

Among top-line UK stocks, shares in Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc led FTSE 100 decliners, each shedding more than two percent after news that LVMH intended to buy all Guinness' interest in their joint ventures.
The move would give France's LVMH the right to continue marketing and distributing Guinness brands in key markets including China, the U.S. and Japan for at least 10 years.
On the currency front, analysts said that while higher Japanese bond yields and the jump in the Nikkei had helped to boost the yen against the dollar, its gains were seen as limited.
The dollar also edged lower against the mark, while the mark itself firmed against other European currencies on worries about economic and monetary union and the French elections.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7000 marks and 115.70 yen compared with 1.7045 marks and 116.50 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 8.2 points, or 0.18 percent, at 4,6743.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 84 points, or 3.13 percent, at 2,596.34.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade down 37.94 points, or 1.03 percent, at 3,636.50. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX was down 24.93 points, or 0.68 percent, at 3,640.50.
PRECIOUS METALS
Palladium was off its record morning fix at $186.00, up $9.75 on news of a strike in South Africa. Platinum was up $2.50 at $399.50 but also off its early high.
Gold fixed at $342.80 vs $344.70 in the morning, while silver was down five cents at $4.70.
